text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Saudi Defence Minister Prince Sultan says Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani is welcomed to visit the kingdom at any time.
- Syria says rapprochement with Iraq is not at the expense of ties with ally Kuwait.
- South Africa's state arms maker Denel is in talks with a Middle Eastern country for a $1.5 billion deal.

- Moslem Sunni Islamist MPs say: Liberals want to bring down the government...this is the point of difference. Liberals and two Sunni political groupings were on opposite sides in Kuwait's elected parliament last week when liberal MPs questioned Finance Minister Nasser Rodhan over alleged violations.
- Yemen owes Kuwait 100 million dinars ($330 million). A team from the state Kuwait Investment Authority flew to Yemen on Sunday to discuss repayment schedule.
- Kuwait to send aid to the Czech Republic after the country was hit by severe flooding.
- Stocks down. The Kuwait Stock Exchange index fell 14.8 points on Sunday to 2,428.
- Kuwait one of the largest re-export markets for Dubai in 1996.
- Qatar's al-Watan newspaper slams Syria's opposition to Doha's hosting in November of a regional economic conference with Israel's participation.
